'''Donta Lamont Smith''' (born November 27, 1983) is an American-Venezuelan professional [[basketball]] player for [[Trotamundos de Carabobo]] of the [[Venezuela]]n [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). Playing for [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]], he was named the 2014 [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP]].

==High school==
Smith played his high school basketball at [[Oldham County High School]], in [[Buckner, Kentucky]], where he was a standout forward on the high school team, and also a record-setting [[wide receiver]] on the [[high school football|football]] team.  He also played on the Kentucky (high school) All-Stars in their annual two-game series against the Indiana All-Stars.

==College career==
After two years of playing junior [[college basketball]] at [[Southeastern Illinois College]], Smith was rated as one of the top [[JUCO]] prospects, and he committed to play [[NCAA Division I]] college basketball for [[Rick Pitino]] at the [[University of Louisville]], with the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]].  However, Smith backed out of the commitment, and entered the [[2004 NBA draft]] instead.

==Professional career==
Smith was taken by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the second round of the [[2004 NBA draft]], after playing [[JUCO]] [[college basketball]] at [[Southeastern Illinois College]], and he averaged 3.3 points per game for the Hawks during his two-season stint. On December 2, 2005, the Hawks assigned Smith to their [[NBA Development League]] affiliate, the [[Arkansas RimRockers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mediacentral.nba.com/login/|title=Media Central Login – NBA Media Central}}</ref>

In January 2007, Smith signed a one-month contract with Bulgarian champions [[PBC Lukoil Academic|Academic Sofia]], which could possibly be extended to five months. On December 24, 2008, Smith signed with the [[South Dragons]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australasia)|National Basketball League]]. He had previously been with the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]'s [[Shanxi Zhongyu]] but was waived to make roster space available for [[Bonzi Wells]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/archive/old-sport-pages/dragons-new-man-cleared-to-play/news-story/791e4d2842e74a4e3697fcc298197c8d|title=Dragons' new man cleared to play|date=December 23, 2008|website=www.heraldsun.com.au}}</ref>

In 2009, Smith went on to win the [[2008–09 NBA season|2009 NBL championship]] with the [[South Dragons]], and was named Finals MVP after starring for the team in the 5-game series. After one season with the [[South Dragons]], Smith would return to the [[Shanxi Zhongyu]] for the 2009–10 season. In December 2010 he signed with the [[Liaoning Dinosaurs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.niubball.com/2010/12/good-to-go-liaoning-signs-its-second-import-donta-smith/|title=Good to go: Liaoning signs its second import, Donta Smith • NiuBBall.com|date=December 10, 2010|access-date=December 11, 2010|archive-date=December 16, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101216040324/http://www.niubball.com/2010/12/good-to-go-liaoning-signs-its-second-import-donta-smith/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2011, Smith signed with [[Fuerza Regia]] in Mexico.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Mexico/basketball.aspx?NewsID=245183|title=Mexican Basketball, News, Teams, Scores, Stats, Standings, Awards - latinbasket|website=www.latinbasket.com}}</ref> He later played for the [[Indios de Mayaguez]] of Puerto Rico,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/basketball.aspx?NewsID=259900|title=Puerto Rican Basketball, News, Teams, Scores, Stats, Standings, Awards - latinbasket|website=www.latinbasket.com}}</ref> and [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] of Israel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basket.co.il/News.asp?id=4755|title=מנהלת ליגת העל בכדורסל | מכבי ת"א, ירושלים, מכבי חיפה ואשדוד בחצי הגמר|website=basket.co.il}}</ref>

Smith led Haifa to its first [[Israeli Basketball Super League|Israeli Super League]] title ever during the 2012–13 season, his first with his team, along with teammate [[Gal Mekel]]. In the following season, 2013–14, Smith was awarded [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|the Israeli Basketball League's Most Valuable Player Award]], after leading Haifa to the finals for the second time in a row. Haifa, however, could not win the title again, after losing the finals to [[EuroLeague]] superpower [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]. In 2014, he was chosen the MVP of the Israeli All-Star game.

In June 2014, after two successful seasons with Haifa, Smith signed a three-year contract with Israeli team [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]]. In his first season with the team, he was instrumental in its winning its first ever national championship. He left Hapoel Jerusalem in July 2016 after losing the opportunity for a second title to [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion BC]].

On November 23, 2017, Smith signed with [[New Basket Brindisi]] for the rest of the [[2017–18 LBA season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/254974/happy-casa-brindisi-signs-donta-smith.html|title=Happy Casa Brindisi signs Donta Smith}}</ref>

On June 4, 2018, Smith signed with [[Santeros de Aguada]] for the rest of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|2018 BSN Season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/america/puerto-rico/275947/donta-smith-signs-with-santeros-de-aguada.html|title=Donta Smith signs with Santeros de Aguada|publisher=Sportando.basketball|date=4 June 2018|access-date=6 June 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On July 9, 2018, Smith signed with the French team [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez]] for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/france/pro-a/280944/pau-orthez-signs-donta-smith.html|title=Pau-Orthez signs Donta Smith|work=Sportando.basketball|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On August 31, 2019, he has signed 3-months deal with [[Levallois Metropolitans]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/metropolitans-sign-donta-smith/|title=Metropolitans sign Donta Smith|date=August 31, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 2, 2019|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> Smith averaged 8.7 points, 4.4 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game.

On July 15, 2020, he signed with [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Forward Donta Smith returns to Maccabi Haifa |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/forward-donta-smith-returns-to-maccabi-haifa/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 15, 2020 |date=July 15, 2020|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref> On March 8, 2021, he was released by the team. In 2020-21 he was third in the Israel Basketball Premier League in three-point field goal percentage (46.0 per cent), but third in turnovers per game (3.0).<ref>{{cite web | url=http://old.scouting4u.com/35,3,0,0/israel-basketball-leaders | title=Israel basketball stats, results, box score, scout report and video online | Scouting4U }}</ref>

On September 23, 2021, Smith signed with [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cangrejeros de Santurce inks Donta Smith |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cangrejeros-de-santurce-inks-donta-smith/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 23, 2021 |date=September 23, 2021}}</ref>

==National team career==
In August 2013, Smith was naturalized as a Venezuelan, in order for him to be able to play with the [[Venezuelan national basketball team]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://noticiaaldia.com/2013/08/donta-smit-se-nacionaliza-y-se-ofrece-para-jugar-con-venezuela/ |title=Donta Smith se nacionaliza y se ofrece para jugar con Venezuela |access-date=2013-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213223210/http://noticiaaldia.com/2013/08/donta-smit-se-nacionaliza-y-se-ofrece-para-jugar-con-venezuela/ |archive-date=2014-12-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played with Venezuela at the [[2013 FIBA Americas Championship]].
